edits.find: Unlike fixed-rate bonds or static interest annuities whose real purchasing power deteriorates during inflationary spikes, high-quality dividend growth equities act as a dynamic hedge. Because premier dividend compounders possess pricing power, they pass escalating input costs to end markets, maintaining operating margins and increasing cash payouts at rates that historically match or exceed consumer price inflation.
edits.replace: Fixed payments, such as those from many bonds, lose purchasing power when inflation rises. Companies with pricing power may be able to raise prices and dividends over time, which can help offset inflation over long periods—but this is not guaranteed. Dividends can lag inflation or be cut, and stock prices can fall when inflation and interest rates rise.
